citations.claim: First violation: body resting on thin top face of wall 0 with distance_to_surface -0.152, i.e. penetration beyond 0.15 limit
Horizontal velocity unchanged from initial, showing no bounce impulse was ever applied
One step before failure body already penetrates (-0.072) with same vx, sinking progressively
Two steps before failure body was still outside wall (+0.007 gap) approaching at shallow angle

counterfactual.change: Thickened the thin plate from h=0.2 (y=8.6) to h=1.0 (y=7.8) keeping the same top face at y=8.8; all else identical for 41 steps. The body then bounces (vy=+10.7) instead of sinking, so no violation.

explanation: Fast shallow-angle graze on a 0.2-thick horizontal plate defeats the impulse/positional correction: the body contacts the top face at step 39 with unchanged vx~46.6, then sinks deeper each step (gap +0.007 -> -0.072 -> -0.152) while vx stays exactly constant and vy keeps falling under gravity, i.e. no bounce impulse or depenetration is applied. With 7 substeps per step the per-substep motion (~0.026) is far below wall thickness, so it is not tunneling through but a failed resting/grazing contact on a thin box. Thickening the wall while keeping the same top face restores the bounce.
vision_note: The red circle makes grazing contact with the top of the thin horizontal wall and stays there instead of bouncing off. By step 41 it is visibly embedded in and intersecting the wall, sunk deeper than in steps 38-40.
